topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the cancer biology lecture series, establishes the learning outcomes, and outlines the scope of the course for students of diverse disciplines.

topics.label: Cellular differentiation, genetic alterations, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer arises from accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal developmental differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological and histological characteristics of tumor invasion and metastasis across the stepwise progression from benign lesions to malignancy.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and mechanisms of disease
topics.groupedBecause: They address how benign and malignant neoplasms are categorized and named, alongside the pathological mechanisms by which they produce morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the frequency and tissue distribution of tumors across human populations, domestic animals, and multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening methods
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the clinical signs of cancer and evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of population screening approaches across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session by reiterating the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping remarks for the upcoming practicals and lectures.
